result:
`./compile.sh` reports success and all three test classes compiled cleanly.

Summary of what was built, under `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/`:

- **`TokenAgentTest`** — constructor initial state (`Type.INVALID`, empty `content`, all booleans false), field mutability, `reset()` restoring the initialized state, `toString()`, and `Token.Type` enum contract (`values()` order/ordinals, `valueOf()` round-trip and its documented exceptions).
- **`LexerAgentTest`** — all the boolean predicates (`isDelimiter`, `isQuoteChar`, `isCommentStart`, `isEscape`, `isEndOfFile`, `isStartOfLine`, `isEscapeDelimiter`, matching the javadoc's own `"[|]"`/`'!'` example), `readEndOfLine`'s documented greedy `\r\n` consumption (verified via `getCharacterPosition()` deltas), escaping behavior and its end-of-stream failure (exercised through `nextToken()`), `trimTrailingSpaces`, and `nextToken()` across simple/quoted/doubled-quote/comment/empty-line/unterminated-quote cases, plus `getFirstEol()` and the byte/char/line counters.
- **`CSVParserAgentTest`** — `parse(String,...)`/`parse(Reader,...)`, the deprecated constructors' documented null-argument `IllegalArgumentException`, `close()`/`isClosed()`, the documented post-close behavior of `iterator()`/`stream()`, the `IOException→IllegalStateException`/`UncheckedIOException` wrapping (via a custom failing `Reader`), `nextRecord()`, header/comment methods, `getFirstEndOfLine()`, and `builder()`.

One real constraint shaped the design: `lib/` doesn't include `org.apache.commons.io`, which `CSVParser.Builder` and the `parse(File|InputStream|Path|URL, Charset, CSVFormat)` overloads depend on transitively (the latter because a private `parse(IOSupplier, ...)` overload shares their arity, so `javac` must resolve `IOSupplier` just to rule it out during overload resolution). Any test touching those fails to compile regardless of what's passed in, so I documented that in a class comment and covered the remaining, compilable surface as thoroughly as the javadoc supports instead (e.g. testing `Lexer`'s escape/end-of-line behavior indirectly through `nextToken()` and `getCharacterPosition()` rather than through `ExtendedBufferedReader` directly, which has the same issue).
